modifications: Unrigged Tripo export in 16 parts (409,478 triangles, three 2048 px textures: base colour, metal/roughness, normal map; one double-sided material), standing on four feet facing -X. Welded across UV seams and the seams between parts (21 edges split at T-junctions, 9 pinholes filled), decimated as one mesh with the head keeping 4.5 times the share of the rest (4,121 of 37,500 triangles: her face is seen close up), and split back into its 16 parts, closed (remake/tools/blender-decimate.py ... detail=4.5, Blender 5.2; kept as source/brontosaurus-parts.glb, which the command reproduces byte for byte). Baked by remake/tools/bake/bake-quadruped.js with kind=sauropod (run with bake-character.mjs): turned to face +X, scaled to 22 m long (8.62 m high), stood on the ground with the root midway between the feet; the parts told apart by position and seams (the head holds the nose, the neck and the front of the body lie on the seams between it and the body, which carries the tail; four legs; the six toenail parts ride their feet, the two flank patches the hips); rigged with 26 bones, the neck's joints spaced along its centre line; welded into one closed, consistently wound skin whose seams share their weights; the texture atlas redrawn so her head gets more of it (atlas=0.82: the rest narrowed to 82 % of the width, the head's 7 islands copied from the 2048 px source into the freed column at 2.09 times their old size, her head 11,348 texels at 1024 px before, 41,816 after); the brow ridges softened (brow=1: 146 vertices over the eyes smoothed along their normals, by 5.9 cm at most, the eyes' outlines untouched); six clips authored in code (sauropod-clips.js); one skinned mesh with one matte single-sided material (roughness 0.62, no metalness, normal map at 0.5), base colour (no recolour) and normal map as 1024 px JPEG, the metal/roughness map dropped. Then the face pass and the mouth pass (below).
rig: Our bake tool for quadrupeds, with kind=sauropod. Bones: root, Hips, Spine, Chest, Neck, Neck2, Neck3, Neck4, Neck5, Head, Tail1-Tail8, and for each leg one rigid bone hanging from the root with the foot below it, named as the engine's footing plants them: BackLeg.L/R, BackFoot.L/R, FrontLeg.L/R, FrontFoot.L/R; the Jaw from the mouth pass under the Head; identity rest rotations. The neck rises at about 45 degrees from the chest (3.8 m up) to the head's joint (7.7 m up), its five joints about 1.07 m apart along its centre line; the skin follows the chain by where it lies along the line through the joints (a point far from the line, the chest under the neck, blends the stretches nearly as close), and the head is rigid in front of its joint. A leg swings from a pivot on its axis at half the height (4.31 m); the skin blends from the leg into the body between the top of the leg part and the pivot, and the body around it follows as a harmonic field. Clips: idle 6.0 s (a slow breath, the neck drifting a little and the head looking about, the tail swinging); walk 3.77 s, 3.88 m a cycle (1.03 m/s; four beats in lateral sequence, a foot down 62 % of the cycle, landing flat and sweeping back at exactly that speed; the hips and shoulders ride as high as their planted legs reach); kink 2.8 s (a friendly nod: the chin lifts, the head dips 24 degrees and then 15, and comes back); lowerHead 4.5 s, played once (the neck curves down in front of her until her eyes are 0.95 m above the ground, a child's eye height, 5.8 m ahead of her fore feet, the face tipped 10 degrees down, and holds); liftUp 8.0 s, played once (from exactly that pose the neck rises slowly to its full height, the eyes 9.4 m up against 8.3 at rest, the head level from a third of the way up, and holds); happy 2.4 s (she rocks back so her front feet leave the ground by up to 0.47 m, comes down with a soft stamp, the front feet a moment apart, and wiggles her neck and tail; the clip keys the legs). lowerHead and liftUp carry once in their extras, so the actor plays them once and holds the last pose. The feet stay planted in idle, kink, lowerHead and liftUp; in a scene the engine's footing plants them in walks, starts, stops and turns on the spot.
pose: Rest pose on four feet, neck raised about 40 degrees, back level, long tail tapering to a whip; faces -X; 0.98 units long, 0.38 high.
sourceTextures: three 2048 px JPEG: base colour, metal/roughness, normal map; one double-sided material
decimateCommand: "C:/Program Files/Blender Foundation/Blender 5.2/blender.exe" -b --factory-startup --python remake/tools/blender-decimate.py -- remake/assets/characters/source/brontosaurus-tripo.glb remake/assets/characters/source/brontosaurus-parts.glb 37500 tripo_part_7 parts detail=4.5
facePass: Eyes found in the colour map by remake/tools/bake/face.js (eyes.js) and written into the GLB as extras on the skinned mesh (face.eyes: per eye its centre, frame, outline and lid and lash colours, in bind space), for the eyelids the engine builds in code (engine/eyelids.js). The eyes are 0.98 m apart, 8.26 m up at rest. Geometry and textures unchanged.
mouthPass: A jaw cut by remake/tools/bake/mouth.js: her lower jaw belongs to the head part, so the pass splits the triangles along her smile (the line given in the head frame, read off a gridded side view, 1.5 cm below the lips' crease, from the corner of the mouth to the chin's front at f = 0.615 m) in front of f = 0, gives the jaw side its own vertices there (94 triangles split, 99 lip vertices opened; snap=0.003 counts vertices within 3 mm of the line as on it, so no sliver stretches across the open mouth), adds a Jaw bone under the Head at the hinge, blends the jaw in from the hinge to the cut, fills the mouth with a pocket (palate and tongue painted into a free corner of the colour map; 1,560 triangles) and writes face.mouth.talk = 8 (degrees the jaw opens at the loudest syllable). No teeth. Re-exported with GLTFExporter (textures 1024 JPEG), node names and clip extras kept.
passes: decimateCommand, then bakeCommand, then faceCommand, then mouthCommand (the bake finds the eyes itself for lowerHead and the brows; the face pass writes them; the mouth pass takes its head frame from them). Rebaking from the parts reproduces the GLB byte for byte.
lookCheck: qa/remake/shots/thorsedla-look/ (the six views, the face, the rig, the clips walk, kink, lowerHead, liftUp and happy, back faces in magenta on the lowered pose; engine/: shut eyes and talking in the scene), qa/remake/shots/thorsedla-brow/ (the brow before and after), qa/remake/shots/thorsedla-mouth/ (the mouth line on a gridded side view, the jaw open 8 and 14 degrees), qa/remake/shots/thorsedla-bench-r1/ and -r2/ (chapter=lineup: lineup, thorsedla, thorsedlaFace, thorsedlaSide) and qa/remake/shots/bronto-look/ (the source as received).
budget: GPU at the tablet preset, 1280x800 on the Iris Xe laptop, __benchmark medians, runs with and without her interleaved in one page load (six rounds each), two loads: she adds 0.1 to 1.0 ms, typically 0.6 to 0.7 (0.3 to 0.7 in the wide lineup, 0.6 to 1.0 with her face filling the frame). Whole frames: the wide lineup with all five characters 6.15 to 6.21 ms (5.53 to 5.83 without her), over 6 ms; her own shots 2.9 to 5.3 ms. Draw calls: she adds 2 (her skin and her quarter-level shadow caster), 55 in the wide lineup. Triangles: she adds 49,016 (her 39,214 and the 9,802 of the shadow caster; at 28.7 m in the wide lineup her bind-pose diagonal of 24.1 m is 645 px on screen, just above the half level's 644 px), so the lineup's shots are 199k to 299k triangles (150k to 250k without her), the wide lineup and her two shots with all five characters in view over 250k. Textures: two 1024 px maps, 56.5 MB in all in the lineup.
notes: Golden yellow body, lighter cream-gold belly, beige throat, caramel cloud-shaped patches along the back, neck and tail, dark toenails, as in the concept; STYLE.md section 3 takes Þórseðla's row from this model. Friendly closed smile, no teeth. The brow ridges read a little stern next to the concept's soft eye: the bake smooths them (brow=1) and the eyelids close in a soft curve. Brontosaurus, as her Icelandic name says (the owner's choice, 2026-10-16, replacing Brachiosaurus). Real adult size: 22 m from nose to tail tip (21 to 22), 8.6 m to the top of the raised head. A later chapter: her head comes down to Egill (lowerHead) and she lifts him into the treetops (liftUp).
